title: Phishing Awareness & Deception Detection
what_is_it: Phishing is a social engineering attack where adversaries impersonate legitimate entities (such as IT support, banks, or executive leadership) to deceive individuals into divulging sensitive credentials, financial data, or triggering malicious links.
why_matters: Over 80% of enterprise security incidents originate with a deceptive email or message. Detecting phishing at the human boundary prevents initial access.
warning_signs: Artificial urgency (e.g., 'Account locked within 1 hour unless verified')
Mismatched sender address or deceptive domain typosquatting
Generic greetings or unexpected attachments (.iso, .zip, .exe, .html)
Unprompted password resets, wire transfer, or gift card instructions
Unexpected QR codes embedded in email bodies (Quishing)
safe_practices: Always inspect full sender domain headers rather than just display names
Navigate directly to known portal bookmarks rather than clicking links in emails
Report suspicious messages to the SOC using the official reporting button
Never approve MFA prompts or enter passwords on unverified domains
what_to_do: If you clicked a suspicious link or provided credentials: Immediately disconnect Wi-Fi/network, notify your SOC/Helpdesk, and reset passwords from a secondary known-clean device.

title: Password Security & Modern Authentication
what_is_it: Password security involves using robust, non-reusable secrets and password managers to prevent credential stuffing and brute-force compromise.
why_matters: Adversaries automate credential stuffing across hundreds of services using compromised databases from third-party breaches.
warning_signs: Reusing the same password across personal and work services
Short passwords under 12 characters or using common dictionary words
Storing passwords in unencrypted spreadsheets or sticky notes
safe_practices: Use passphrases of 4+ random words or 16+ randomized characters
Adopt an enterprise-approved password manager
Never share administrative or personal credentials over chat or email
Migrate to FIDO2 Passkeys where supported
what_to_do: If you suspect a password leak, immediately change it across all shared accounts and verify active login sessions.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) & Fatigue Defense
what_is_it: MFA requires two or more verification factors (knowledge: password, possession: hardware key/authenticator app, inherence: biometrics) before granting access.
why_matters: MFA blocks over 98% of automated credential stuffing attacks. However, attackers attempt MFA push bombing to exhaust users into approving requests.
warning_signs: Sudden flood of mobile authenticator push notifications when you are not logging in
Caller claiming to be IT asking for your 6-digit one-time code
SMS-based codes requested by strangers on WhatsApp or Telegram
safe_practices: Prefer FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys or number-matching authenticator apps over SMS
Deny and report any unprompted push notification immediately
Never dictate one-time codes to anyone, including IT personnel
what_to_do: Report repeated unprompted MFA requests to your SOC as an active credential spraying or MFA fatigue incident.

title: Social Engineering & Pretexting Awareness
what_is_it: The psychological manipulation of individuals into performing actions or divulging confidential information through authority, fear, greed, or helpfulness.
why_matters: Attackers target human psychology because it bypasses perimeter firewalls and encryption algorithms.
warning_signs: Callers demanding immediate non-standard procedures under the guise of an executive
Tailgaters attempting to follow you through secure building access turnstiles
Requests to bypass standard purchase order or verification flows
safe_practices: Verify unusual requests via an out-of-band communication channel
Politely request visitor badges and escort unfamiliar guests
Follow standard organizational verification protocols without exceptions
what_to_do: Document details of the interaction and report the pretexting attempt to Corporate Security.

title: Safe Browsing & Web Threat Recognition
what_is_it: Practices and controls designed to avoid malicious websites, drive-by downloads, malvertising, and deceptive web portals.
why_matters: Web browsers interact with external untrusted content continuously, making them primary delivery vehicles for exploits and infostealers.
warning_signs: Pop-ups claiming 'Your computer has 5 viruses! Call this number'
Suspicious file downloads (.scr, .bat, .iso) triggered without clicking download
Browser warning pages regarding expired or invalid SSL/TLS certificates
safe_practices: Keep browsers updated to the latest stable release
Enable browser sandboxing, enhanced tracking protection, and ad blocking
Do not bypass browser HTTPS certificate warning prompts
what_to_do: Close the suspect browser tab immediately, clear cache, and run an endpoint scan.

title: Secure Wi-Fi & Public Network Hygiene
what_is_it: Ensuring data transmissions are encrypted and protected against eavesdropping and evil-twin access points when working on untrusted networks.
why_matters: Unencrypted or spoofed public hotspots allow attackers to intercept traffic, spoof DNS, or inject malicious payloads.
warning_signs: Open public Wi-Fi networks with generic names ('Free_Airport_WiFi') requiring no password
Device prompting unexpected captive portals asking for social media credentials
Browser warnings about DNS redirects when joining hotel or cafe networks
safe_practices: Always connect through an enterprise or trusted VPN on public networks
Disable automatic Wi-Fi joining for open networks
Turn on WPA3 or WPA2-Enterprise for home and office networks
what_to_do: Disconnect immediately, forget the network, and turn on cellular hotspot.

title: Software Updates & Patch Management Awareness
what_is_it: The timely application of vendor security patches to operating systems, firmware, browsers, and enterprise applications.
why_matters: Over 60% of network breaches exploit known vulnerabilities for which a patch was already released but delayed in deployment.
warning_signs: Repeatedly dismissing 'System Restart to Update' reminders for weeks
Running deprecated or unsupported software versions (e.g., Windows 7, Python 2)
Unapproved third-party utilities downloaded without IT review
safe_practices: Enable automatic security updates for operating systems and key applications
Reboot workstations weekly to ensure patch installation finishes
Uninstall unused browser plugins and legacy tools
what_to_do: Report software requiring legacy compatibility to IT so compensating controls can be established.

title: Ransomware Defense & Extortion Awareness
what_is_it: Ransomware is malicious software that encrypts an organization's files and exfiltrates proprietary data, demanding payment for decryption keys.
why_matters: Ransomware attacks halt business operations, compromise patient care, and inflict severe financial and reputational losses.
warning_signs: Mass file extensions changing unexpectedly (e.g., document.pdf.locked)
Files failing to open and unexpected README_RESTORE text files appearing on desktop
Endpoint fans running at maximum while CPU usage spikes from rapid disk operations
safe_practices: Maintain offline, immutable 3-2-1 backup copies of critical data
Enforce least-privilege permissions on shared network drives
Never disable endpoint protection or EDR agents
what_to_do: Immediately pull physical Ethernet cables and turn off Wi-Fi. Do not power down the machine (preserves volatile memory for forensics), notify SOC immediately.

title: Removable Media & USB Device Safety
what_is_it: Managing risks associated with USB flash drives, external hard disks, and malicious USB hardware (such as Rubber Ducky keystroke injectors).
why_matters: Unattended USB drives dropped in parking lots or lobbies can bypass network firewalls via physical human curiosity.
warning_signs: Finding an unlabeled USB drive in common areas, elevators, or conference rooms
Plugging in a flash drive and seeing unexpected command prompt windows flicker
safe_practices: Never insert unknown USB drives into work or personal computers
Hand discovered removable media directly to Corporate Physical Security
Use corporate cloud sharing repositories rather than thumb drives
what_to_do: If an unknown USB was inserted, disconnect machine from network immediately and inform the SOC.

title: Data Privacy & Sensitive Information Handling
what_is_it: Protecting Personally Identifiable Information (PII), intellectual property, and health records in accordance with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA.
why_matters: Data exposure leads to regulatory fines, loss of customer trust, and weaponized extortion by threat groups.
warning_signs: Exporting customer databases to unencrypted personal thumb drives or email accounts
Setting cloud storage buckets or shared folders to 'Public / Anyone with the link'
Pasting proprietary source code or customer data into public consumer AI tools
safe_practices: Classify and label sensitive information (Confidential, Restricted)
Encrypt sensitive data both in transit (TLS) and at rest (AES-256)
Adhere to organizational acceptable-use guidelines when using generative AI tools
what_to_do: Notify your Data Protection Officer (DPO) and security team within 24 hours of discovering unauthorized data exposure.

title: Mobile Device Security & App Hygiene
what_is_it: Securing smartphones and tablets that access corporate email, VPNs, and authentication tokens.
why_matters: Mobile devices travel into untrusted environments daily and often store active session tokens for corporate clouds.
warning_signs: Apps requesting unnecessary permissions (e.g., calculator app requesting contacts/SMS)
Unexpected rapid battery drain or high data consumption without usage
Prompts to install configuration profiles from third-party websites
safe_practices: Only install apps from official stores (Google Play, Apple App Store)
Enable biometric lock and automatic remote wipe after failed attempts
Keep mobile OS updated and never jailbreak/root devices used for work
what_to_do: Revoke suspicious app permissions and initiate a remote wipe if device is lost.

title: Remote Work & Home Office Security
what_is_it: Securing hybrid work environments that operate outside the corporate perimeter firewall.
why_matters: Home routers and smart IoT devices often run outdated firmware, creating pivot opportunities for intruders.
warning_signs: Leaving home Wi-Fi routers on default manufacturer admin passwords ('admin/admin')
Allowing family members or guests to use corporate-issued laptops
Leaving work screens unlocked when stepping away in public co-working spaces
safe_practices: Change default admin passwords on home routers and create a guest network for IoT
Lock computer screens (Win+L / Cmd+Ctrl+Q) whenever stepping away
Use privacy screens when working in coffee shops or airport lounges
what_to_do: Report any lost work laptop or unmonitored home network intrusion to your SOC immediately.

title: Cloud Account Security & Access Control
what_is_it: Defending cloud identities, API keys, and administrative consoles in environments like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
why_matters: Cloud credentials committed to public code repositories can be harvested within minutes by automated adversary scrapers.
warning_signs: Hardcoded API keys or secrets found in git commits or public repositories
Assigning broad Administrator privileges when read-only access is sufficient
Cloud accounts lacking mandatory MFA enforcement
safe_practices: Use secret managers and environment variables instead of hardcoded strings
Enforce Least Privilege and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Review access logs and enable CloudTrail/Cloud Audit logs
what_to_do: Rotate compromised API keys immediately and invalidate existing session tokens.

title: Incident Reporting & SOC Escalation Protocol
what_is_it: The structured process by which employees swiftly notify security teams of anomalies, mistakes, or suspicious observations.
why_matters: Early reporting dramatically shortens the dwell time of attackers, often turning a catastrophic breach into a minor contained event.
warning_signs: Hesitating to report a clicked phishing link out of fear of disciplinary retribution
Attempting to manually clean malware or delete suspicious logs without notifying SOC
safe_practices: Embrace a blameless reporting culture: rapid reporting protects the whole organization
Know the emergency SOC contact hotline, email, and internal chat channel
Preserve evidence: take photos of error messages, note timestamps, and do not reboot
what_to_do: Contact the SOC within 15 minutes of an anomaly: state What happened, When, and on Which device.

title: AI-Enabled Scam & Deepfake Awareness
what_is_it: Recognizing modern threats powered by generative artificial intelligence, including voice cloning, deepfake video calls, and hyper-personalized spear-phishing.
why_matters: AI tools allow adversaries to generate grammatically flawless lures and clone executive voices in real time.
warning_signs: An urgent phone call from an executive or relative demanding immediate wire transfer with slight audio artifacts
Video call participant whose facial expressions or lip sync appear unnatural or glitch when turning their head
Emails referencing obscure personal trivia extracted from social media scraping
safe_practices: Establish pre-agreed verbal safe words or out-of-band verification procedures for financial transactions
Ask the caller unexpected challenge questions that only the authentic person would know
Never bypass Dual-Authorization financial controls based on verbal or video requests alone
what_to_do: Hang up, verify via a secondary direct channel, and inform the Security Operations Center.
